overview: KLA Corporation is the dominant global supplier of process control, process-enabling and yield-management equipment, software and services used by semiconductor, specialty-semiconductor and PCB/electronics manufacturers. Formed in 1997 from the merger of KLA Instruments and Tencor Instruments, KLA sells inspection, metrology and chemistry-process-control systems that detect and characterize nanometer-scale defects across wafer, reticle, IC, packaging and PCB fabrication. The company is organized into three segments -- Semiconductor Process Control (~90% of revenue), Specialty Semiconductor Process, and PCB and Component Inspection -- and derives roughly 87% of revenue outside the U.S., with China, Taiwan and Korea its largest markets.

business_model.summary: KLA sells capital equipment (inspection/metrology/patterning tools) to chipmakers building and expanding fabs, plus a growing, largely recurring services business (maintenance, support, subscription-like service contracts tied to the installed base) that accounted for ~23% of FY2026 revenue. Product revenue is driven by customers' capex cycles and technology-node transitions (EUV, advanced packaging, high-bandwidth memory); service revenue scales with the size and utilization of the installed base and grew 16% in FY2026 even as product demand fluctuates with the cycle.
business_model.customer_type: B2B -- concentrated base of leading-edge foundry/logic, memory and specialty-semiconductor manufacturers plus PCB/substrate makers; TSMC has exceeded 10% of total revenue in each of FY2024-FY2026
business_model.geographic_mix: China 29.8%, Taiwan 26.8%, Korea 13.5%, North America 13.0%, Japan 6.7%, Europe & Israel 5.4%, Rest of Asia 4.8% (FY2026, by ship-to location); international revenue ~87% of total

competitive_position.market_position: Dominant leader in semiconductor process control/inspection; management has cited process-control share around 58% in 2025 (up ~360 bps since 2021), roughly several times the share of its nearest competitor. KLA is far more concentrated in process control than diversified equipment makers like Applied Materials (deposition/etch) and ASML (lithography), and does not compete head-to-head with Lam Research.

moat_factors.description: Once a fab qualifies a KLA tool for a given production line, switching to a competitor requires costly re-qualification; this entrenches KLA across successive nodes and drives durable, high-margin service attach.
Over 9,100 active patents plus ~3,600 pending; R&D spend (~11% of revenue, $1.5B in FY2026) funds continuous leadership in inspection/metrology that smaller rivals struggle to match.
Direct sales, applications-engineering and service organizations across Asia, the U.S. and Europe support complex, customer-specific tool configurations and long-term relationships.

As nodes shrink (2nm) and advanced packaging/HBM proliferate, more inspection/metrology steps are required per wafer, structurally growing KLA's served market faster than overall wafer fab equipment spend.

weaknesses: High customer concentration -- a small number of leading-edge foundry/logic and memory customers (led by TSMC) drive a large share of orders
Significant and growing exposure to U.S.-China export control actions, which have already cut China revenue from 43% (FY2024) to 30% (FY2026) of total
Highly cyclical demand tied to semiconductor capex, with limited visibility into the durability of the current AI-driven investment surge
Leveraged balance sheet ($5.95B senior notes) with capital increasingly directed to buybacks/dividends rather than net debt reduction

growth_drivers: AI/HPC-driven leading-edge logic and memory capex (2nm foundry/logic, HBM/advanced DRAM) requiring higher process-control intensity per wafer
Advanced packaging growth -- management has cited advanced-packaging process-control revenue approaching/exceeding $1B annually, up sharply year over year, as AI compute drives more complex packages
EUV lithography adoption in high-volume manufacturing, which creates new inspection/metrology requirements
Record backlog ($12.57B at FY2026-end, up from $7.86B a year earlier) providing revenue visibility into FY2027
Services revenue growth from an expanding, aging installed base of tools (16% growth in FY2026)
Continued legacy/mature-node investment from automotive, industrial and IoT electrification trends
Capital return program -- 17 consecutive years of dividend increases and $9.74B of remaining buyback authorization as of June 2026

business.description: A small number of leading-edge manufacturers (TSMC >10% of revenue each of the last three fiscal years) drive outsized order volatility; loss or delay of a single customer's program can materially affect results.

Capital equipment orders are highly cyclical and tied to customer capacity decisions; backlog does not reliably indicate timing of revenue recognition, and elevated AI-driven spending may not be sustained.
Applied Materials and ASML have greater aggregate financial and R&D resources and could bundle competing capabilities or undercut pricing.
Customers could reduce inspection/metrology sampling rates or disruptive manufacturing technologies could reduce KLA's served market.

financial.description: $5.95B of senior notes outstanding; covenant compliance and credit-rating maintenance depend on continued strong cash flow; buybacks have been partly debt-financed.
Exposure to yen, euro, pound sterling and new Israeli shekel; hedges may be inadequate in periods of large currency moves.
Supplier DRAM-chip shortages drove higher purchase commitments in FY2026 and are expected to pressure gross margin into FY2027.

regulatory.description: Successive BIS rules (2022-2025) and the 2025 'Affiliates Rule' (suspended until Nov 2026) restrict sales/service to Chinese advanced-node customers; management estimated a $300-350M revenue headwind through CY2026, and China's revenue share has fallen from 43% (FY2024) to 30% (FY2026).

U.S. tariffs have raised cost of revenues; a February 2026 Supreme Court ruling invalidated IEEPA-based tariffs, creating uncertainty over refunds and future presidential tariff authority; a Section 232 investigation into semiconductor imports is pending.
China controls ~70% of rare-earth mining and ~90%+ of processing/magnet manufacturing; 2025 Chinese export controls on rare earths could constrain KLA's component supply.
2025 U.S. tax reform (OBBBA) and OECD Pillar Two global minimum tax could materially change KLA's effective tax rate.

macro.description: A large share of recent growth is tied to AI-driven data-center and leading-edge investment; a slowdown in hyperscaler/AI capital spending (a fear that drove a broad semicap sell-off in early November 2026) would disproportionately hit KLA's leading-edge exposure.
Fixed-to-floating interest rate swaps on $2.0B of notes and a floating-rate revolver create some exposure to rate moves; portfolio investments are also exposed to rate-driven mark-to-market losses.
Significant KLA manufacturing/R&D operations in Israel and heavy customer concentration in Taiwan expose the company to regional conflict risk.

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Semiconductor capital equipment spending is expected to remain elevated through FY2027, driven by AI/HPC-related leading-edge logic and memory investment and advanced packaging; management expects continued revenue growth into fiscal 2027 and third-party estimates put the wafer fab equipment market above $200B in 2027.
macro_factors.cyclicality: High -- historically cyclical in line with semiconductor manufacturers' capital equipment procurement patterns, though the growing services mix (23% of revenue, recurring) partially smooths the cycle.
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate -- indirectly through customer capex financing costs and directly through $2.0B of notes swapped to floating rate and investment portfolio mark-to-market.

recent_developments.event: KLA fell roughly 13% in a single session amid a broad semicap sell-off (also hitting Applied Materials and Lam Research) driven by investor concern that AI/data-center capital spending could slow; stock down ~30% from its early-August 2026 high through November 6.

Reported fiscal Q1 2027 results: revenue of $4.14B (+29% YoY), beating the midpoint of prior guidance; non-GAAP diluted EPS of $1.22, GAAP EPS of $1.18. Guided fiscal Q2 2027 revenue to $4.7B +/- $200M and non-GAAP EPS to $1.44 +/- $0.11.
Effected a 10-for-1 stock split and proportional increase in authorized shares; all share/per-share figures in recent filings are split-adjusted.

Board increased the share-repurchase authorization by $7.00B; by June 30, 2026 the company had repurchased $2.29B of stock and paid $1.06B of dividends during the fiscal year, with $9.74B of buyback authority remaining.

Commerce (BIS) issued an interim final rule (the 'Affiliates Rule') expanding export-control obligations to foreign entities majority-owned by listed parties; BIS suspended the rule for one year (until November 2026), easing near-term compliance burden but leaving it as an overhang.
China imposed new export controls/licensing requirements on additional rare-earth elements, a potential supply-chain risk for KLA's component sourcing.
Record backlog of $12.57B (up from $7.86B a year earlier) on AI-infrastructure-driven demand; FY2026 revenue of $13.58B (+12% YoY), net income of $4.83B, gross margin 61.3%.

items.notes: Implies continued sequential growth after Q1 FY2027 revenue of $4.14B (+29% YoY), which itself beat the midpoint of prior guidance of $4.0B +/- $200M.
Compares with Q1 FY2027 non-GAAP EPS of $1.22.
Compares with Q1 FY2027 GAAP EPS of $1.18.
FY2026 full-year gross margin was 61.3%; management has flagged DRAM component cost inflation and tariffs as ongoing margin headwinds into FY2027.

Qualitative guidance from the FY2026 10-K Executive Summary: 'we expect continued revenue growth as customer engagement and demand signals continue to strengthen.' No formal full-year numeric guidance has been issued; KLA guides one quarter at a time.

guidance.management_commentary: Management has characterized demand as broad-based across leading-edge foundry/logic and memory customers, driven by AI/HPC infrastructure buildout, with advanced packaging a particular growth standout. Management also flagged DRAM component shortages/cost inflation and tariffs as gross-margin headwinds expected to persist into fiscal 2027, and said China revenue should continue to decline as a share of the total due to export-control restrictions even as legacy-node investment by domestic Chinese customers continues.

bull_case: Structurally dominant, high-margin position in semiconductor process control (~58% share) with strong switching-cost and installed-base moats
AI-driven leading-edge logic/memory capex and advanced packaging are expanding KLA's served market faster than overall wafer fab equipment spending
Record backlog ($12.57B) and 29% YoY Q1 FY2027 revenue growth provide visibility into continued near-term growth
Growing, recurring services revenue (23% of sales, +16% YoY) cushions cyclicality and supports margin durability
Disciplined capital returns -- 17 consecutive years of dividend increases plus a large ($9.74B) buyback authorization -- following a 10-for-1 split that improves share liquidity/accessibility
bear_case: Stock fell ~30% from its August 2026 high amid fears that AI/data-center capex growth is set to slow, and valuation (still ~34x trailing earnings as of early November 2026) leaves little room for a demand disappointment

Escalating U.S.-China export controls have already cut China's revenue share from 43% to 30% over two years and remain an unpredictable, worsening overhang (including a still-pending 'Affiliates Rule')
High customer concentration (TSMC alone >10% of revenue) and historic industry cyclicality mean a pause in leading-edge investment could hit orders and backlog quickly
Rising DRAM component costs, tariffs and a leveraged balance sheet ($5.95B notes) are near-term margin and capital-allocation headwinds
Backlog by KLA's own admission 'does not provide meaningful information about the timing of future revenue recognition,' so order cancellations/push-outs could surprise investors
